free_tier.stated: OpenVZ-512 at USD 3.49/month: 1 CPU, 512 MB RAM plus 512 MB vSwap, 20 GB SSD, 1 TB bandwidth, SolusVM panel, 1 IPv4 and 1 IPv6, in Los Angeles, Dallas, Mumbai/Pune, Paris or Quebec. The page states "Plans starting at $3.49/Month", with the same plan at USD 10.47 quarterly, USD 20.94 semi-annually and USD 41.88 annually. The tracker lists a cheaper row, OpenVZ_256 at USD 2.00/month billed yearly (1 Intel core shared, 256 MB RAM, 10 GB HDD, 256 GB/month, 0.1 Gbps, Los Angeles) and states "starting at $24.00 per year", but no 256 MB plan appears anywhere on the vendor page read, so this record leads with the plan the vendor actually sells.

egress.terms: bandwidth is a plan line item, 1 TB a month on OpenVZ-512, with no overage rate and no post-quota shaping policy published on the page read

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.tooling: root OpenVZ container with a SolusVM panel and TUN/TAP/PPP enabled, so any client runs inside it and no wrapper is needed; the vendor documents no API on the page read. OpenVZ is container virtualisation, not KVM, so the kernel is shared and a custom kernel module will not load.
record.chaining: At USD 41.88 a year this holds a public IPv4 with root and a SolusVM panel, which makes it a DNS secondary, a mail relay or a cron box; 512 MB of RAM and 20 GB of disk cannot hold a working set, and 1 TB a month moves control traffic only, so the data path belongs on a volume-quota host or an unmetered one.

record.category: vps (hosted, Los Angeles, KVM, IPv4 and IPv6)

free_tier.stated: No free tier. KVM 1GB is USD 17.99 a year (about USD 1.50 a month) on annual billing until 8 November 2026: 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 20 GB NVMe, 2TB/month of bandwidth, Los Angeles. The standing KVM ladder starts at USD 3.99 a month (KVM-512: 512 MB, 15 GB SSD, 1 TB premium bandwidth, 1 IPv4 and 1 IPv6 address).

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a virtual server, not an object store

retention.stated: not applicable: a live server, not stored bytes

egress.terms: 2TB/month on KVM 1GB and 1 TB/month on KVM-512, on a premium port of 1-10Gbps; extra bandwidth is sold at USD 2.00 a month per 1 TB. No overage rate and no post-allowance policy is published on the pages read.
egress.price_per_tb: USD 2.00 per 1 TB per month (KVM upgrade add-on)

record.interface_detail: Root SSH on a full KVM guest; SolusVM or Virtualizor panel on the standing ladder, a VPS control panel and Docker Manager on the Diwali plans.
record.tooling: ssh, any VPN or tunnel daemon the guest kernel supports; the OpenVZ line states TUN/TAP/PPP.
record.chaining: A KVM guest with one IPv4 and one IPv6 address per plan is a UDP-capable endpoint in Los Angeles; the pages read state no NAT, no port-forward count and no inbound filter, and no routed IPv6 prefix (one IPv6 address is listed).
record.binding_note: 2TB/month is the only published ceiling on KVM 1GB; the first failure for a high-volume job is the allowance, after which extra bandwidth is a USD 2.00 a month add-on per 1 TB.

identity_cost.detail: unverified: the client-area register page says an account is made by placing an order, and the order-form fields were not read; the pages list 'Multi Currency Payment Supported & Accepted' without naming a method.

record.reliability_note: The annual price is a promotion that ends on 8 November 2026; the renewal price is not stated on the pages read.
record.confidence_note: The price, the 2TB/month allowance and the IPv4 and IPv6 lines are vendor sentences read on 2026-11-03. Identity, the renewal price and whether the IPv6 line is one address or a prefix are not stated, so the record is not raised above documented for those fields.
